_description: Therapeutic-area-aware developability profiles. For a candidate indication we pick a profile from the disease's therapeutic area (or the user's area filter), then judge the molecule's RDKit-computed physicochemical properties against the ranges that matter for THAT route of delivery. Edit ranges/weights freely; add new profiles and map areas to them under 'area_to_profile'. Property rule: value within [ideal_min, ideal_max] => ideal (1.0); within [acceptable_min, acceptable_max] => acceptable (0.6); otherwise out (0.0). Missing bound = unbounded on that side. Score = weighted mean of property statuses.

topical_dermal.label: Dermatology — topical (skin permeation)
topical_dermal.rationale: Stratum-corneum penetration favours low molecular weight and moderate lipophilicity (the 'rule of 500'); excessive logP or H-bonding strands the molecule in the skin.

topical_ocular.label: Ophthalmology — topical (corneal permeation)
topical_ocular.rationale: The cornea is a lipophilic–hydrophilic–lipophilic sandwich, so balanced logP and adequate aqueous solubility (for the tear film) matter more than raw lipophilicity.

cns_oral.label: CNS / Neurology — oral (BBB penetration)
cns_oral.rationale: Blood–brain-barrier penetration requires low polar surface area, modest size and lipophilicity, and few H-bond donors.

inhaled_respiratory.label: Respiratory — inhaled (lung deposition)
inhaled_respiratory.rationale: Inhaled drugs favour moderate size and lipophilicity for dissolution and retention in the airway lining fluid without rapid systemic absorption.

oral_systemic.label: Oral / systemic — Lipinski Rule-of-Five
oral_systemic.rationale: Oral bioavailability is well predicted by Lipinski's Rule-of-Five plus polar surface area and rotatable-bond count (Veber).
